topic: Himalayan River Systems: Ganga, Indus, Brahmaputra
description: The Himalayan river systems are perennial, fed by both snowmelt and precipitation. They primarily comprise three major river basins: the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra, which hold immense geographical, economic, and cultural significance for the Indian subcontinent.

sections.title: Key Characteristics of Himalayan Rivers
sections.description: Himalayan rivers are distinct in their origin, flow patterns, and the geological landforms they create.

key_concepts.explanation: Rivers that existed before the upliftment of the Himalayas. As the mountains rose, these rivers maintained their courses by cutting through the rock, forming deep gorges. Examples include the Indus, Sutlej, and Brahmaputra.
These rivers flow throughout the year as they receive water from two sources: the melting of Himalayan glaciers in summer and monsoon rainfall in the rainy season.

important_facts.fact: Himalayan rivers are currently in their youthful stage, engaging in vigorous erosional activities and forming spectacular V-shaped valleys, rapids, and waterfalls.

sections.title: The Indus River System
sections.description: The Indus is one of the largest river basins in the world, flowing through Tibet (China), India, and Pakistan.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Bokhar Chu Glacier near Mansarovar Lake, Tibet
geographical_data.key_characteristics: In India, it flows only through the Union Territory of Ladakh. It eventually drains into the Arabian Sea near Karachi, Pakistan.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Bara Lacha La Pass, Himachal Pradesh
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the largest tributary of the Indus. Formed by two streams, Chandra and Bhaga, it is also known as Chandrabhaga in Himachal.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Beas Kund near Rohtang Pass, Himachal Pradesh
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the only major tributary of the Indus system that flows entirely within the geographical borders of India.
It is an antecedent river that enters India through the Shipki La pass. The famous Bhakra Nangal Dam is built on it.

historical_events.significance: A water-distribution treaty brokered by the World Bank between India and Pakistan. India got exclusive rights over the three eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej).

sections.title: The Ganga River System
sections.description: The Ganga is the largest river system in India, holding the highest cultural reverence and supporting the densely populated Northern Plains.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It originates as the Bhagirathi. It is the longest river in India with a total length of 2,525 km.
The longest and westernmost tributary of the Ganga. It runs parallel to the Ganga and joins it at Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj.
An antecedent river infamous for shifting its course frequently, which causes devastating floods, earning it the title 'Sorrow of Bihar'.

key_associations.extra_info: It is at this confluence that the river officially takes the name 'Ganga'.
One of the highly revered Panch Prayags (five confluences) in Uttarakhand.

important_facts.fact: The Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers combine to form the Sundarbans Delta in the Bay of Bengal, which is the largest and fastest-growing delta in the world.

sections.title: The Brahmaputra River System
sections.description: The Brahmaputra is one of the largest rivers in the world in terms of water volume, flowing through Tibet, India, and Bangladesh.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Chemayungdung Glacier of the Kailash range, Tibet
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It flows eastwards parallel to the Himalayas, takes a sharp U-turn at Namcha Barwa, and enters India through a deep gorge.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Middle of the Brahmaputra River in Assam
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the largest riverine island in the world and the first island in India to be made a district.

key_associations.extra_info: The name of the Brahmaputra in Tibet, which translates to 'The Purifier'.
The name by which the river is known when it first enters India in Arunachal Pradesh.
Upon entering Bangladesh, the Brahmaputra is known as the Jamuna before it merges with the Padma (Ganga).

important_facts.fact: Major tributaries of the Brahmaputra include the Teesta, Subansiri (the largest tributary), Manas, and Lohit.
